result.topic_en: Conclusion of a proof of a reciprocity law for the biquadratic (quartic) residue symbol between two primary Gaussian primes m and M, showing that the product of the two symbols equals a sign ε = ±1 determined by the parities of b/2 and B/2.
result.transcription:
folglich
$\left(\frac{m}{M}\right)\left(\frac{M_1}{m_1}\right) = i^{\frac12(aA+bB-1-A-a+2)} = i^{\frac12((a-1)(A-1)+bB)}$
$= i^{\frac12 bB}$ also $\pm1$ je nachdem $\frac12 b, \frac12 B$ $\left|\begin{array}{l}\text{nicht beide ungerad}\\ \text{beide ungerade}\end{array}\right.$
$= \varepsilon$

Also
$\left(\frac{m}{M}\right) = \varepsilon\left(\frac{M}{m}\right)$ W.Z.B.W.

methods.what: Product of the quartic residue symbols of two primary Gaussian primes expressed as a power of i
Simplification of the exponent: the sign is ±1 according to whether b/2 and B/2 are not both odd or both odd
